## Significance

Delayed detection increases recovery time because responders act on incomplete traces. Earlier detection may reduce failed retries and shorten incidents.

## Innovation

The study combines trace data with controlled fault injection, allowing the same failure to be observed under repeatable load conditions.

## Approach

We will first reproduce the fault with the [test protocol](./protocol.md) and remove invalid traces using the criteria defined there, then compare three detection rules using the same traces, report precision and recall with 95% confidence intervals, and record processing time for each rule so operational cost can be compared; if fewer than 200 valid traces remain after filtering, we will treat the comparison as exploratory rather than confirmatory.
expected:
## Significance

Delayed detection increases recovery time because responders act on incomplete traces. Earlier detection may reduce failed retries and shorten incidents.

## Innovation

The study combines trace data with controlled fault injection, allowing the same failure to be observed under repeatable load conditions.

## Approach

1. We will reproduce the fault with the [test protocol](./protocol.md).
2. We will remove invalid traces using the criteria defined in the protocol.
3. We will compare three detection rules using the same traces.
4. We will report precision and recall with 95% confidence intervals and record processing time for each rule so operational cost can be compared.

If fewer than 200 valid traces remain after filtering, we will treat the comparison as exploratory rather than confirmatory.
